name: ProntoQA
intro: ProntoQA是一个合成的问答基准，旨在通过基于一阶逻辑的测试用例和思维链来评估大型语言模型的多跳推理能力。该数据集能够将生成的思维链解析为符号证明，以进行形式化分析，从而系统地探究语言模型的推理能力。研究发现，虽然模型在单个演绎步骤上表现良好，但在需要系统探索多个有效选项的证明规划方面存在困难。
build_method: 从3至10概念的线性本体生成唯一肯定前件证明，再用受控语法翻译为问答与标准思维链
task_type: 判断题, 思维链生成
eval_feature: 反向语义解析模型思维链并逐步判断有效性、原子性与是否偏离标准证明路径
scale: 按配置动态生成；论文主实验每个配置400个测试样例，覆盖1、3、5跳并使用8-shot提示
build_method_en: Generate a unique chained-modus-ponens proof from a linear ontology of 3-10 concepts, then translate it into QA and gold CoT with a controlled grammar
eval_feature_en: Semantically parse model CoT back into logic and classify each step by validity, atomicity, and deviation from the gold proof path
intro_en: ProntoQA is a synthetic question-answering benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' multi-hop reasoning abilities through first-order logic-based test cases and chains of thought. The dataset allows generated chains of thought to be parsed into symbolic proofs for formal analysis, enabling a systematic investigation of the models' reasoning capabilities. Studies show that while models perform well on individual deductive steps, they struggle with proof planning that requires systematically exploring multiple valid options.
scale_en: Generated per configuration; the paper's main experiments use 400 test examples per setting across 1, 3, and 5 hops with eight-shot prompting
drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-18; status=source-reconstructed-awaiting-independent-signoff; scope=final ICLR PrOntoQA paper and the paper-matched official v1 code branch, explicitly excluding later PrOntoQA-OOD behavior. Primary evidence is https://arxiv.org/pdf/2210.01240v4 with SHA-256 8e0502fa3b6b93c967441b99270bb4ec0bcdd37924502eaa128ad0e7a6e567d9. Code evidence is asaparov/prontoqa origin/v1 commit 066f73fc70bfaa92ed2476fd3c41b4951ad6e63a dated 2023-05-23; the default main commit 0a6412b6fddf46324a1cb96e066dd7b3d89b87d6 includes later OOD work and is therefore not used as the primary implementation source. The v1 tree includes LICENSE with Apache-2.0, model_outputs.zip, the generator, prompt runner, semantic grammar, proof evaluator, and analysis scripts. Dataset construction was checked against paper sections 3 and A.2. The task deliberately restricts reasoning to repeated modus ponens with Ax and Hop rules and generates one unique gold proof from a small linear hierarchy. The ontology has 3-10 concepts, subtype edges and node properties, with every node having zero or one child. Fictional ontologies use invented names to suppress pretraining knowledge; true ontologies sample from three hand-coded real ontologies; false ontologies use real concept names in a random, likely counterfactual hierarchy. A starting node is chosen uniformly, an entity-type axiom is created, and the generator walks upward until the requested proof length ends at a node or property. The controlled grammar translates every ontology edge/property and the proof into easy-to-invert language. The initial entity fact is rendered, then with probability 0.5 the query asks whether the proof conclusion is true or whether its negation is false. Each formal conclusion becomes one gold-CoT sentence. The ontology context is fully rendered and ordered first: preorder yields top-down context, while postorder yields bottom-up context that follows the gold proof order. Only after that ordering is complete, the shortcut control uses the generated proof's conclusion property: because its mere appearance nearly reveals the label, the generator creates a novel concept disconnected from the ontology, assigns it the negated conclusion property, and inserts the resulting distractor sentence at a random position in the ordered context. Each on-demand record contains context, query, gold CoT and label with a one-to-one symbolic mapping. Evaluation was checked against paper section 5.1: the controlled factors are 1/3/5 hops, top-down versus bottom-up order, and fictional/true/false ontology. Every prompt contains eight independently and identically generated fully labeled demonstrations and one test question with CoT and label omitted. The paper greedily decodes six GPT-family variants from text-ada-001 through text-davinci-002. The response is split into predicted CoT and final true/false label. A recursive-descent parser maps every predicted sentence back to a logical form; unparseable steps are incorrect. Step validity is strict, broad or invalid; atomicity distinguishes one-rule steps from skipped multi-rule steps; utility marks an off-gold conclusion from gold-proof premises as misleading. A proof is correct when a path connects premises to the target conclusion, even if unrelated invalid steps occur elsewhere. The four proof metrics are strict, skip, broad and valid proof accuracy, reported separately from label accuracy and broken down by hops, context order, ontology, step types and first errors with Wilson 95% intervals. The paper runs 400 examples per configuration and states 48 experiments in the main analysis, whereas the pinned v1 code defaults to 500 trials, sweeps hops 1-through-5 in increments of one, and fixes seed 62471893; the diagram exposes this configuration drift instead of conflating code defaults with paper runs. The release is generated on demand rather than a single immutable row corpus. EN/ZH specifications share identical positioned topology, use no edge labels, and render provenance links dashed. Strict Draw.io/XML and runtime visual review are required next; formal assets and paper_aligned registration remain gated on independent reviewer approval.
